text:
Maya: Heads up — we're proposing to deprecate the current long-lived SIEM export landing buckets and switch to ephemeral, case-scoped extracts for external consumers. Planning doc: https://go/redwood/sec/ephemeral-exports (draft).
Devin: Can you call out the main drivers? cost, compliance, or just access control complexity?
Maya: Short version: (1) cost and data minimization, (2) reduce blast radius from leaked long-term keys, (3) make forensics request flows auditable via short-lived KMS unwraps.
Oliver: Sounds good. How will this affect ongoing investigations that currently expect 90d raw exports?
Maya: We'll keep internal cold archives for 7y as required, but external SIEM consumers will only get timeboxed extracts tied to a JIRA case id + scoped KMS unwrap. Forensic access to raw archives will remain via our analyst JIT playbook.
Zoe: Who needs to approve RBAC changes? I assume ProdSRE, Legal, and Compliance?
Devin: Yep — ProdSRE for infra, Security for policy, Compliance for retention exceptions. We should use the standard repo flow: eng RFC -> security review -> compliance signoff.
Maya: Proposed RBAC change: remove broad splunk-export role and replace with per-consumer ephemeral role. Example policy snippet for the token broker: 
```
resource "redwood_export_role" "case_scoped" {
  name = "export-case-${case_id}"
  actions = ["create_extract"]
  ttl = "24h"
  allowed_indices = ["logs-prod-app-*"]
}
```
Devin: Nice. How do we do KMS integration for unwrap so we can revoke if needed?
security-bot: Reminder: KMS grants must be short-lived and logged. See policy KMS-UNWRAP-001. Audit events will be emitted to audit-log-cluster.
Oliver: And rotation? We should rotate the export broker signing key quarterly and support emergency revocation.
Maya: Agreed. Action items: create RFC, update RBAC roles, add KMS unwrap audit stream, update forensic playbook, and run a dry-run with one partner.
Zoe: I'll own RFC and compliance coordination. ETA for RFC PR: EOW?
Maya: EOW works. Devin, can you scope the infra tasks and list required tickets?
Devin: I'll open tasks under INFRA-EXPORTS: 1) token-broker auth changes, 2) KMS unwrap logging hook, 3) export TTL enforcement in gateway, 4) ephemeral-signer rotation. ETA next Tue.
Oliver: For vuln triage: any change that adds broker or unwrap code needs threat modeling and a focused pentest signoff. Adding to the RFC checklist.
Maya: Good call. Also tagging this for incident response playbook updates — add a sample forensic timeline when an ephemeral extract is compromised.
Compliance: We'll need a documented exception path for partners that legally require longer retention; must include legal attestation and audit windows.
Maya: Thanks — I'll include exception template and evidence requirements. Can we do a dry-run with Partner X next month?
Devin: Put Partner X on the test plan. I'll coordinate with partner-ops.
Oliver: One more note: update alerting so any export > 24h TTL raises a P1 to security oncall.
Maya: Done — will include in the RFC and link to alert runbook.
Zoe: LGTM, creating PR now. :thumbsup: 
Maya: Thanks team. Will post RFC link here when ready and ping for review.
